rules.statement: Every accepted lifecycle transition records actor, reason, source revision, resulting revision, and event time.
A stable request identity converges on one scientific effect when its content fingerprint remains identical.
Custody position, custody event, and pending integration message become visible through one transaction boundary.
Raw bytes, content digest, parsed observation, disposition, and recovery owner remain linked.
Sapio qualification binds tenant release, SDK release, schema fingerprint, service identity, and independent readback.
Benchling event processing commits durable inbox work and retrieves authoritative resource state when freshness matters.
LabKey validation, commit, audit reason, normalized readback, lineage, and artifact parity form one conformance tranche.
Migration gates evaluate identity, canonical content, relationships, audit, signatures, artifacts, exceptions, and rollback.
A clean-environment restore reconstructs records, metadata, audit, signatures, artifacts, configuration, and approved recovery objectives.
Identity, authorization, tenant, retention, and redaction decisions remain attributable and testable.

Environment-scoped workload identities resolve non-secret configuration from AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store and rotating secret material from AWS Secrets Manager; KMS context, version stage, cache bounds, redacted retrieval telemetry, and repository build state log and fixture reference posture remain testable.
Operational measures preserve numerator, denominator, threshold, window, and evidence locator.
Every instant uses an explicit offset at ingress, one UTC canonical representation, declared precision, and distinct business occurrence and server recording meanings.
Internal identity, external tenant-source identity, and content digest use distinct validated primitives with explicit namespace, algorithm, canonicalization, and content scope.
Every scientific quantity binds finite decimal precision, raw and canonical values, analyte, assay or method revision, UCUM unit, qualifier, limits, and conversion provenance.
Controlled vocabularies, strict versioned JSON, and status-dependent nullability preserve one unambiguous representation for each accepted state.
Every tenant-owned row participates in tenant-preserving referential integrity and forced default-deny row-level security derived from authenticated context.
Domain events, signatures, corrections, and status transitions append through controlled boundaries and preserve original meaning through explicit supersession.
Aggregate state, immutable event, and outbox intent commit together; Debezium routes committed outbox records and consumers apply stable idempotency keys.
Representative workloads determine indexes, query-plan objectives, retention keys, and measured partition thresholds for high-growth laboratory and evidence relations.

A supported PostgreSQL major, immutable versioned SQL set, migration-product checksummed history, database-scoped coordination, catalog projection, and predecessor upgrade evidence define database release state; Flyway Community 13.0.0 is the selected implementation profile.
Expand, backfill, reconcile, converge, contract, and recovery phases preserve compatibility across independently deployable application releases.
Migration reconciliation evaluates identity, structure, scientific semantics, relationships, distributions, artifacts, audit history, tenant security, and exceptions.
A database release identifies the data contract, Flyway migration set, resulting catalog, reconciliation result, security result, concurrency result, recovery result, and known limitations.
